intro: Buying a home in Minnesota means planning for more than your monthly loan repayment. Local property taxes, homeowners insurance, winter heating expenses and maintenance costs can all influence how much house you can comfortably afford.

Our free Minnesota mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and mortgage term. Whether you're purchasing in Minneapolis, Saint Paul, Rochester, Duluth or a smaller Minnesota community, compare financing options and establish a realistic budget before making an offer.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Minnesota?

blocks.markdown:
A $330,000 Minnesota home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed interest rate would cost approximately $1,582.81 per month in principal and interest.

Here is an illustrative monthly payment breakdown.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. The interest rate, taxes and insurance premiums are illustrative rather than current statewide averages.

Minnesota offers housing opportunities across metropolitan neighborhoods, suburban developments, university communities and rural areas.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Minnesota housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/MN/HSG860222), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $329,300 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $1,947, while 72.2% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical statistics include homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions. They should not be interpreted as current mortgage quotes or property asking prices.

Housing prices around the Twin Cities can differ from those in smaller communities. Buyers should investigate recent comparable property sales, local employment access and recurring ownership expenses before establishing a purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Minnesota Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your property and the amount you plan to contribute as a down payment.

Select your preferred repayment period and enter your lender's quoted annual interest rate. If you haven't received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national reference.

Next, enter annual property taxes, homeowners insurance and monthly association fees. Include private mortgage insurance where required.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and experiment with different financing arrangements.

The amortization schedule shows how your mortgage balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay throughout the repayment period.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare borrowing scenarios outside Minnesota.

sections.heading: How Minnesota Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Minnesota property taxation involves property valuations, classifications, applicable exclusions, local tax rates and other adjustments.

The county assessor determines the property's estimated market value. Qualifying exclusions can reduce that amount before property classification rates are applied.

The resulting tax capacity helps determine the property's share of applicable local tax levies. Certain other taxes and assessments may be calculated differently.

### Minnesota Homestead Market Value Exclusion

Qualifying homeowners may benefit from the [Minnesota Homestead Market Value Exclusion](https://www.revenue.state.mn.us/homestead).

The current calculation provides the following benefits:

The maximum exclusion is $38,000.

Some older online guides still reference a maximum exclusion of $30,400 and a lower phaseout threshold. Buyers should use the current rules applicable to their assessment year.

### Minnesota property tax calculation example

Consider a qualifying homestead with an estimated market value of $330,000.

The market value above $95,000 is $235,000. Multiplying this difference by 9% produces a reduction of $21,150 from the maximum exclusion.

This example calculates taxable market value, not the final property tax bill.

For ordinary Class 1a residential homesteads, the classification rate is generally 1% on the first $500,000 of taxable market value and 1.25% on the remaining value.

These classification rates determine tax capacity and should not be mistaken for the effective annual property tax rate.

Consult your county assessor for an estimate that incorporates applicable local levies and other charges.

### Applying for homestead classification

According to the [Minnesota Department of Revenue's homestead classification guidance](https://www.revenue.state.mn.us/homestead-classification), applicants generally need to own the property, occupy it as their principal residence and be Minnesota residents.

Applications are normally due to the county assessor by December 31 for taxes payable the following year.

Eligible exclusions are applied automatically once the appropriate classification is established.

### Minnesota property tax refunds

Minnesota also offers [property tax refund programs](https://www.revenue.state.mn.us/property-tax-refund) for qualifying homeowners.

Regular refunds depend on household income and property taxes. Special refunds may be available to homeowners experiencing qualifying tax increases.

These refunds should not automatically be deducted from monthly mortgage escrow estimates because eligibility and payment timing vary.

Minnesota properties can experience hailstorms, thunderstorms, tornadoes, heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures.

Insurance premiums depend on replacement costs, roof condition, property location, construction materials and coverage requirements.

Request several property-specific quotes before committing to a home purchase.

### Wind and hail deductibles

Some homeowners policies contain separate wind and hail deductibles.

For example, a 2% deductible based on $300,000 in insured dwelling coverage would represent $6,000 in potential out-of-pocket expenses for an applicable covered claim.

Ask insurers whether roof damage is covered at replacement cost or depreciated value.

The [Minnesota Department of Commerce's homeowners insurance guidance](https://mn.gov/commerce/insurance/home/) explains important coverage distinctions and potential exclusions.

### Flood and water backup coverage

Ordinary homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding.

Homeowners with basements should also investigate coverage for sewer backups and sump pump failures. These risks may require separate endorsements.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate flood exposure.

Include applicable additional insurance premiums in your annual housing estimate.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, 6% fixed annual interest and a 30-year mortgage.

These figures exclude taxes, insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare the complete monthly housing expenses rather than principal and interest alone.

Minnesota Housing offers mortgage financing and assistance through participating lenders.

### Start Up mortgage program

The [Minnesota Housing Start Up program](https://www.mnhousing.gov/home/homeownership/buy-home-refinance) primarily serves eligible first-time buyers.

For one-unit properties, purchase price limits effective July 1, 2026, are $515,200 in the designated 11-county metropolitan area and $472,030 elsewhere in Minnesota.

Household income, property eligibility, credit and homebuyer education requirements also apply.

### Step Up mortgage program

Step Up provides financing options for qualifying repeat buyers and certain first-time buyers who exceed Start Up limits.

The corresponding one-unit purchase limits are $515,200 in the designated metropolitan area and $498,257 elsewhere.

Review the [official Minnesota Housing purchase price limits](https://mnhousing.gov/lenders-and-partners/homeownership-lender-toolkit/purchase-price-limits) before selecting a property.

### Down payment and closing cost assistance

Minnesota Housing offers several forms of secondary financing.

The Monthly Payment Loan requires repayment over 15 years at the associated first mortgage interest rate.

Deferred loans carry no scheduled monthly payments or interest, but borrowers remain responsible for repayment when applicable conditions occur.

These arrangements are loans rather than unconditional grants. Compare their complete financing terms before applying.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Minnesota Home

blocks.markdown:
Winter heating expenses can materially affect household budgets, especially for older properties with inefficient insulation or heating equipment.

Request historical utility bills and inspect the condition of furnaces, windows and roofing.

Homeowners should also budget for snow removal, driveway maintenance and emergency repairs.

Rural properties may involve private wells, septic systems and access road maintenance.

Condominium buyers should review association reserves, recurring dues and proposed special assessments.

These expenses extend beyond the calculator's standard mortgage payment estimate and should be included in your broader financial plan.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Minnesota?

blocks.markdown:
Start with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial commitments.

Our [Minnesota Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/minnesota-paycheck-calculator/) can help estimate after-tax earnings, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate outstanding borrowing obligations.

Allow sufficient room for groceries, transportation, childcare, utilities and retirement savings.

Compare mortgage offers using the [CFPB Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/) and maintain an [emergency fund](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) for insurance deductibles and unexpected repairs.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $330,000 Minnesota home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, principal and interest would be approximately $1,582.81 monthly. Property taxes, insurance and other applicable expenses increase the total payment.

### What is Minnesota's Homestead Market Value Exclusion?

It reduces the taxable market value of eligible homestead properties. The maximum exclusion is $38,000, with the benefit gradually decreasing for properties valued above $95,000 and disappearing at $517,200.

### Does Minnesota offer down payment assistance?

Yes. Minnesota Housing provides eligible borrowers with secondary financing of up to $18,000 through designated assistance programs. Available amounts, repayment arrangements and qualification requirements vary.

Use our Minnesota mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, down payments, interest rates and loan terms.

Replace illustrative expenses with accurate local property taxes and insurance quotes. Consider heating, maintenance and emergency savings when determining whether a property fits your long-term financial goals.
